iss_keypoints — 3D feature_register op

• Data kinds: points → indices

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.iss_keypoints(points, radius, nms_radius=None, gamma21=0.99, gamma32=0.99, max_kp=400, min_neighbors=8) (to call the implementation directly, import feat_shot; feat_shot.iss_keypoints(points, radius, nms_radius=None, gamma21=0.99, gamma32=0.99, max_kp=400, min_neighbors=8); from the registry, ops3d.get("iss_keypoints"))

Usage

ISS (Intrinsic Shape Signatures, the 3-D Harris equivalent) keypoint detection.

Uses the minimum eigenvalue λ3 of the local covariance as saliency, takes as candidates only points whose eigenvalues are distinct (orientation well-defined), and selects them sparsely with NMS. Rotation-invariant. Returns = an array of point indices.

Arguments:

• points (N,3). radius: radius of the neighbourhood sphere for saliency (same units as the point cloud).

• nms_radius: distance for non-maximum suppression. None means 0.6*radius.

• gamma21, gamma32: upper limits of the eigenvalue ratios λ2/λ1, λ3/λ2 (default 0.99). Only points where both are below

this are candidates (excludes points whose ratio is close to 1 = isotropic, with undetermined orientation).

• max_kp: maximum number returned. min_neighbors: points with fewer neighbours than this are not candidates (default 8).

Procedure: for each point, gather the neighbours within radius and compute the eigenvalues λ1≥λ2≥λ3 of the 2nd-order moment matrix (qᵀq)/n with the point of interest as origin (excluded if λ1 is 1e-12 or less). Scanning in descending order of λ3 as saliency, a greedy NMS discards points closer than nms_radius to an already accepted point. Returns an int64 array of point indices (descending saliency). Length 0 if there are no candidates.

Note: neighbours are centred on the point of interest (not on the centroid), so even for points on a plane λ3 does not become exactly 0. It is a Python loop doing a neighbourhood search for every point, so clouds above tens of thousands of points should be thinned with voxel_grid_downsample before use. It feeds directly into the keypoint input of shot_descriptor, and register_shot calls it internally with 0.6× radius and NMS 0.3×.
